nodes.name: Solution deposition and calcination
nodes.procedure: First, we prepared thin-film surfaces with metal precursors on polycrystalline Ni pellets via solution deposition. Subsequently, metals were deposited on Ni with rapid calcination (hereinafter, the blend of M and Ni is denoted as M/Ni, where M is the sacrificial metal (M = Sn, Zn, Al, or Pb)).
nodes.source_text: First, we prepared thin-film surfaces with metal precursors on polycrystalline Ni pellets via solution deposition. Subsequently, metals were deposited on Ni with rapid calcination

nodes.name: Magnetron sputtering
nodes.procedure: We deposited a Pb thin film on a Ni pellet (Pb/NP) and a Ni foam (Pb/NF) electrode by simple magnetron sputtering. The thickness of the sputtered Pb films was determined to be ≈10 nm by X-ray reflection spectroscopy.

nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 2a, the bare Ni catalyst exhibited a 278 mV overpotential at a current density of -10mAcm^{-2} before the RC flow. The HER performance of the bare Ni catalyst deteriorated with an overpotential of 310 mV after the 10th RC cycle due to its oxidation by the RC flow.

nodes.source_text: The HER performance of the Pb/Ni catalyst exhibited continuous improvement during repeated RC cycles, with a 231mV overpotential achieved after the 10th RC cycle (Figure 2a; Figure S3, Supporting Information). The HER current density at the 10th RC cycle for the Pb/Ni catalyst at -0.25V versus RHE was -14.1mAcm^{-2}

nodes.description: Long-term CV RC cycling stability test (700 cycles) in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: To further confirm the durability of the RC-Pb/Ni-based electrode for HER during repeated RC cycles, 700 RC cycles were implemented with CV measurement (≈12.6 h, Figure S6, Supporting Information). ... Remarkably, the overpotential of the Pb/Ni catalyst at 5mAcm^{-2} gradually decreased from 243mV to 221mV and saturated after the 700th cycle.

nodes.characterization_summary: fcc-Ni diffraction peaks at 2θ = 44.4°, 51.7°, 76.3°, 92.8°, 98.3° (JCPDS 04-0850); dominant (220) peak at 76.3° broadened and negatively shifted for Pb/Ni indicating Pb incorporation into Ni matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For both the bare polycrystalline Ni and the Pb/Ni catalysts, fcc-Ni diffraction peaks at 2θ = 44.4°, 51.7°, 76.3°, 92.8°, and 98.3° (JCPDS 04-0850) were observed. The dominant (220) plane peak of fcc-Ni at 76.3° was broadened and exhibited a negative shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM analysis shows polished polycrystalline Ni electrodes have flat and smooth morphology, whereas Pb/Ni catalyst layer before and after RC flow exhibits relatively rough surfaces, with no distinguishable morphological changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To reveal the morphological characteristics of the Pb/Ni catalyst before and after the RC flow, we additionally conducted scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis. At top-view SEM images of the catalysts, the polished polycrystalline Ni electrodes exhibited a flat and smooth morphology, whereas the Pb/Ni catalyst layer before and after the RC flow exhibited relatively rough surfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Ni and Pb distributed throughout the electrode surface forming two separate layers; quantitative analysis reveals 15.75 wt% Pb overall, 23.49 wt% in upper layer, 8.40 wt% in lower layer before RC, and ≈1 wt% Pb overall, 1.61 wt% in local regions after 10th RC cycle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We then investigated the compositional change of the Pb/Ni catalyst under the RC conditions with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping. ... According to the quantitative composition analysis from the EDS results, the entire sample region included 15.75 wt% of Pb ... After the 10th RC cycle, ≈1 wt% of Pb was distributed throughout the sample, and 1.61 wt% of Pb remained in a local region.

nodes.characterization_summary: O1s spectra under 0.1 mTorr H2O: H2O_ads peak intensity Ni < RC-Ni < RC-Pb/Ni; Pb/Ni shows enhanced H2O_ads and OH_ads vs UHV indicating water dissociation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In a 0.1 mTorr H2O atmosphere, the intensity of the peak assigned to adsorbed water (H2O_ads) increased in the order of Ni < RC-Ni < RC-Pb/Ni ... Pb/Ni exhibited enhanced peak intensities for both H2O_ads and OH_ads in the 0.1 mTorr H2O atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows Ni^0 at 852.28 eV for Ni, Ni(OH)2 at 854.94 eV for RC-Ni; RC-Pb/Ni shows decreased Ni^0 intensity with 0.15 eV negative shift. Pb 4f XPS shows positive shift for RC-Pb/Ni indicating charge transfer from Pb to Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ex situ XPS spectra for Ni 2p and Pb 4f were obtained. Figure 5a compares the Ni 2p XPS core level signals ... the metallic Ni^0 peak exhibited a negative shift (0.15 eV) for the RC-Pb/Ni catalyst ... the Pb 4f XPS spectra (Figure 5b) of RC-Pb/Ni show that the binding energy of metallic Pb^0 positively shifted after the RC flow.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray reflection spectroscopy determines the thickness of sputtered Pb films on Ni pellet (Pb/NP) and Ni foam (Pb/NF) electrodes to be ≈10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of the sputtered Pb films was determined to be ≈10 nm by X-ray reflection spectroscopy (Figure S8, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS detects only 4.2 ppb Pb ions in KOH electrolyte after 10th RC cycle, indicating negligible Pb dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the concentration of the dissolved Pb ions in the electrolyte solution was measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Following the 10th RC cycle, only 4.2 ppb of Pb was detected in the KOH electrolyte.
